# Staying in the loop

## The idea

Aevum does a lot for you quietly in the background — closing your weekly tax bill,
watching your budgets, importing your statements. The activity feed is where all of
that surfaces, so nothing important happens without you knowing.

It's the single place to answer one question: **is there anything I should look at?**

## What shows up

The feed gathers up the moments worth your attention as they happen:

- **A new bill** — your weekly tax bill has closed and is ready to settle.
- **A budget breach** — you've gone over a limit you set.
- **A failed import** — a bank statement couldn't be read and needs another try.
- **Setup left half-done** — something like account security you started but didn't
  finish.
- **Quiet good news** — a bill paid, a task completed.

## Two kinds of update

Not everything in the feed is equally urgent, so Aevum sorts each update into one of
two kinds:

- **Notifications** simply tell you something happened — a bill was generated, a
  payment went through. Nothing is required of you.
- **Alerts** are things that need you to act — an over-budget category, a broken
  import, an unfinished setup step. These sit higher and stand out.

The difference matters because of what happens next: an alert **clears itself the
moment you fix the underlying thing.** Sort out the over-budget spending or finish the
setup step, and the alert quietly disappears on its own — you never have to tidy up the
feed by hand.

## Seen, but not gone

Glancing at the feed and acting on something are different things, and Aevum keeps them
apart:

- Scrolling past an update just **quietens** it — it stays, a little dimmer.
- Acknowledging it settles it for good.
- You can also **snooze** an update, and it'll resurface later when it's a better time.

So a busy week never makes you lose track of something just because you saw it in
passing.

## You decide what's worth hearing

Every kind of update can be **switched off individually.** If new-bill notices are
noise to you but budget alerts aren't, mute the one and keep the other. Your choices are
yours alone, and you can change them any time from your notification settings.

## Always up to date

Most updates appear the instant they happen — the second your weekly bill closes or a
budget tips over. A few are about the passage of time itself, like a payment falling
due, and Aevum checks for those once a day so they never slip through. Either way, the
feed is the one place that always reflects where things stand right now.
